newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold steady in Europe, PGM trade slow and nervous.
newsitem.headline: Gold steady in Europe, PGM trade slow and nervous.

text.p: Gold prices were quoted unchanged from their previous close in early Monday European trade as attention remained locked on platinum group metals (PGMs).
Gold was quoted at $344.20/$344.70 an ounce. Activity was generally quiet with investors sidelined by uncertainty after massive price surges in PGMs, traders said.
Hong Kong, Australian and South Korean markets were closed.
Palladium was quoted higher at $225.00/$245.00, versus $219.15/$229.15, after it traded at 17-year highs last week.
Platinum was a fraction lower than Friday's London close, but at $470.00/$500.00 versus $475.00/$505.00 in London Friday was still pricey. It hit seven-year highs last week.

"At the moment the market is extremely quiet. PGMs are still at high levels," said one trader, adding that markets continued to wait to see if Russian producers and Japanese consumers can arrive at an agreement on PGM deliveries.
Russia, the world's largest palladium supplier and a major platinum producer, has not delivered any metal so far this year. Japan is the world's largest consumer of PGMs.
"Everything depends on that (the agreement)," the trader said. He said that several firms who were short the metals were still having to pay enormous sums to borrow PGMS to meet delivery.
He said the interest rates for palladium remained at 300 percent, and at 150 percent for platinum.
Silver was lower at $4.81/$4.83 versus $4.86/$4.88 in London.
